harmonicFunction: Ab5 (I) - Piercing tonic chord anchoring the furious, defiant punk tempo
Db5 (IV) - Subdominant chord providing explosive forward drive on the 5th string

Eb5 (V) - Dominant chord delivering the rapid turnaround snap back to tonic Ab5

techniques.name: High-Speed Syncopated Power Riffing
techniques.description: Executing rapid, percussive power-chord downstrokes at 186 BPM with precise fret-hand muting between syncopated chord stabs to create explosive rhythmic dynamics

notes: Grip standard root-5th-octave power chords on the 6th and 5th strings
Deliver aggressive, compact downstrokes driven strictly by wrist rotation
Release fret-hand finger pressure immediately on rests for razor-sharp staccato cutoffs
Lock precisely with the snare backbeat to keep the 186 BPM tempo from rushing
sequence: Strike Ab5 on fret 4 of low E string three times
Shift to Db5 on fret 4 of A string
Snap to Gb5 on fret 2 of low E string
Turn around on Eb5 (fret 6 of A string) with snappy pick attack
tips: Billie Joe used a 1956 Gibson Les Paul Junior with a single dogear P-90 pickup into a Park 75 head
Keep your forearm completely loose to prevent muscle cramping at high tempo
Do not drag your pick: keep pick depth shallow across strings 6, 5, and 4
details.progression: Ab5 - Db5 - Gb5 - Db5 - Ab5 - Eb5

techniques.name: Octave Lead Phrasing & Pick Tremolo
techniques.description: Playing melodic octave shapes on strings 5 and 3 while muting the intervening 4th string with the pad of the index finger, providing singing clarity and aggressive garage-punk punch

notes: Place index finger on the root note (string 5) and pinky on the octave (string 3, two frets higher)
Rest the fleshy underside of the index finger lightly against string 4 to completely mute it
Strum aggressively across strings 5, 4, and 3 without fear of string noise
Slide octave shapes smoothly along the neck to trace the vocal melody
sequence: Fret Ab octave at fret 11 (string 5) and fret 13 (string 3)
Slide down to Gb octave (fret 9 and 11)
Walk down to F octave (fret 8 and 10), then resolve to Eb octave (fret 6 and 8)
Execute rapid sixteenth-note tremolo strumming on the climax
tips: Ensure the high E and B strings are also muted by the relaxed flat fingers of the fret hand
Octaves naturally double your presence in a mix without needing a second guitar track
Keep your pick angle slightly slanted to glide effortlessly across the three strings

sections.name: Intro Solo Riff & Full Band Explosion
sections.description: The immortal opening: Billie Joe's P-90 pickup rips through two cycles of the main riff in raw, dry isolation before Tré Cool and Mike Dirnt detonate into the track at 186 BPM.
sections.progression: Ab5 - Db5 - Gb5 - Db5 - Ab5 - Eb5
notes: Play isolated first two cycles completely dry and in-your-face
Sharp syncopated cuts between chord stabs
Full band explodes on the third cycle with crash cymbals
Relentless 186 BPM forward drive

notes: Huge unmuted power chords ringing with punk defiance
Drive downstrokes with maximum pick velocity

sections.name: Guitar Solo Octave Melody
sections.description: Billie Joe unleashes an energetic, singable octave guitar solo, cutting through the mix with raw P-90 crunch and aggressive tremolo picking.
notes: Fret octave shapes on strings 5 and 3
Mute string 4 completely with the pad of the index finger
Slide aggressively between frets 6, 8, 10, 11, and 13
Finish with frantic sixteenth-note tremolo strumming

sections.name: Outro Climax & Feedback Cutoff
sections.description: Furious final chorus repetition with blistering drum fills, ending on a barrage of syncopated unison hits and a sharp amplifier cut.

Full band unison syncopated punches on beat 4
Sudden dead silence on the final chord cutoff
Zero decaying trail: punchy, violent finish

beginner.title: Power Chords & Basic Progression
steps: Learn Ab5, Db5, Gb5, and Eb5 power chord shapes
Practice transitioning between strings 6 and 5 at 120 BPM

intermediate.title: Accelerating to 186 BPM & Syncopated Stops
steps: Accelerate the main riff in 10 BPM increments up to 186 BPM
Master the instant fret-hand muting on the syncopated rests
Develop relaxed wrist stamina for uninterrupted punk downstrokes

advanced.title: The Octave Solo & Full Song Performance
steps: Master the string-muting technique on octave shapes across strings 5 and 3
Execute the high-speed tremolo picking during the solo climax
Perform the entire track with explosive, unyielding punk energy

commonMistakes: Using elbow motion instead of wrist oscillation, which locks up the pick hand at 186 BPM
Letting unplayed strings ring during octave playing, creating awful dissonant mud
Rushing ahead of the beat on the syncopated Gb-to-Db transition
Pressing too hard with the fret hand, causing cramping and finger fatigue
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Wrist rotation warm-up and alternate picking speed bursts
10 mins: Main riff metronome repetition at 120, 150, and 186 BPM
10 mins: Octave muting and slide drills across frets 6 through 13
10 mins: Full speed rhythm play-through focusing on explosive chorus transitions
focusAreas: Pick-hand wrist economy and muscle relaxation at high speed
String 4 muting with index finger pad during octave soloing
Razor-sharp staccato cutoffs on syncopated rests
metronomeWork: Start the intro riff at 130 BPM with a metronome to guarantee clean note separation
Advance tempo by 8 BPM once 4 consecutive flawless cycles are played
Practice muting all strings instantly on sudden rhythmic stops
